analysis: The only changes in docs/architecture/inference.md are the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new documentation section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' (head lines 4816-4826). It says GPT-OSS plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound, up from MLX's defaults of 40-50. It also says results do not depend on the partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX's defaults. This is prose only. No code, key handling, attestation, coordinator-provider protocol, encryption or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The surrounding text (pipeline batching, SSD prefix record encoding, KV precision, manifest pins) is unchanged context. I looked at it against T-041 (prefix cache and at-rest records), TB-007 and TB-002 and found no new claims weakening those controls. The described tuning (`GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers`, `CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding`) lives in source files that are not supplied. Its effect on GPU memory pressure or availability (T-029/T-010 style DoS) and its claim of partition-independent results cannot be verified here. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. I do not see a documentation drift that needs a threat-model update, since the doc makes no secrecy or isolation claims. The doc also states that cluster qualification gates remain separate and does not claim production readiness.
